A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BC-LLM research work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, algorithms, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial revisions and reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original MIMIC simulations, bird-classification and OOD experiments, and hospital readmission results with clinician feedback.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical studies and adds expanded bird comparisons, alternative-LLM experiments in Appendix D, and numerical clinician ratings.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3 retain the same keyphrase-based proposals, split-sample multiple-try sampling, concept annotation, and posterior prediction procedure. Warm-starting and Laplace approximation also remain. Probabilistic annotations were already allowed in v1 Appendix E; revised explanations and example prompts do not establish an underlying method change.

E1.justification: CUB coverage expands from seven selected classification tasks in v1 Section 4.3 to 37 family-level tasks covering the 200 species in v2 Section 4.1. OOD evaluation broadens from the Bunting dog/finch case to unseen species for each bird classifier. The MIMIC and hospital domains remain.

E2.justification: The bird comparison adds Human+CBM using 312 human-annotated features and LLM+CBM (No keyphrases) using 370 LLM-suggested concepts. ResNet also enters the reported OOD comparison. One-pass summarization, Boosting, and Oracle match the renamed LLM+CBM, Boosting LLM+CBM, and Human(Oracle)+CBM; those renamings are not additions.

E3.justification: v2 adds accuracy and Brier reporting, replacing log likelihood in the main MIMIC and hospital displays. It introduces Command-R and Claude 3.5 Haiku configurations, broadens the OOD testing procedure, and adds a blinded clinical-relevance survey using shuffled features and 1–3 ratings. The existing training splits and concept budgets are largely retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds comparisons testing dependence on the LLM backend (Appendix D) and a no-keyphrase control examining concept generation (Table 1). It expands the hospital case study with clinician ratings and revises OOD analysis with broader unseen-species testing and per-concept annotations for the costumed dog.

E5.justification: v1 Section 4.2 explicitly reports four MIMIC replicates; v2 omits this information, including from Appendix E.2. Both retain 95% confidence intervals. This is reduced run-count reporting, not evidence that fewer runs were performed.

E6.justification: v1's per-family bird AUCs and specific dog/finch entropy entries are replaced by aggregate results under expanded coverage, preventing direct before-and-after performance comparisons. Bunting concept posteriors change, and alternative-LLM results and clinician ratings of 2.5 versus at most 2.1 are added. Hospital AUC remains 0.64; new Brier scores round to 0.14 for both BC-LLM and Boosting. Command-R results show lower concept precision for BC-LLM than LLM+CBM despite higher AUC.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.1, its assumptions, and the principal appendix derivations remain substantively unchanged. v2 corrects the concept precision/recall definitions from nonmembership to membership probabilities. It also omits v1 Appendix I's concluding argument extending stationarity to the multiple-try sampler by marginalizing over the sampled subset.

C1.justification: The Bayesian concept-discovery, consistency, and multimodality contributions remain. v2 adds an explicit query-cost comparison against fixed concept banks, qualifies black-box superiority in the abstract as occurring in certain settings, and drops v1's explicit claim to be the first Bayesian LLM framework for learning CBMs.

C2.justification: v2 develops a substantial new discussion of soft-concept information leakage and interpretable annotation, linking uncertain dog annotations to human auditing. It interprets the added Human+CBM comparison and ResNet's higher OOD entropy, discusses ambiguity among correlated smoking concepts, and states that BC-LLM is designed primarily for approximately 20 or fewer concepts.

D1.justification: v2 adds an image-keyphrase prompt, the clinician survey instructions and instrument, and more specific text-versus-image runtime descriptions. Core hyperparameters and the code link were already provided. Conversely, v1's dated GPT-4o-mini identifier, hospital identity, explicit 30-day unplanned-readmission definition, and clinician affiliation/coauthor disclosure are not retained.

R1.justification: Sections 1–2 substantially expand positioning against soft CBMs and label leakage, adding works by Mahinpei, Margeloiu, Havasi, Ragkousis, and Makonnen. v2 connects the acceptance ratio to O'Hagan's partial Bayes factors and supplies Levin et al. and Vershynin references for previous proof citation placeholders. The explicit priority claim is removed.

P1.justification: v2 extensively rewrites the introduction and method motivation, reorganizes the naive updates and split-sample explanation, and places bird experiments before MIMIC. Example prompts are consolidated under Appendix C, and concept-matching instructions move into the appendix. These are substantial narrative and structural revisions.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. Table 1 switches from family rows and method columns to method rows and metric columns. The Bunting figure is redesigned, MIMIC panels are rearranged, and Figure 4 gains clinician-rating bars and highlights. Figure 5 and Tables 2–3 are added.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for the accuracy–interpretability claim by addressing limited bird coverage and missing CBM controls, testing additional LLMs, and supplementing qualitative clinician feedback with blinded ratings. These validation gains outweigh reduced per-task, replicate, and provenance reporting. Important qualifications remain: Command-R concept precision is weaker, and Figure 4 claims a Brier advantage despite rounded ties and reports an unexplained BC-LLM interval of 0.12–0.62.
